items.title: Fossil fuels are climate action. Pipelines are nature protection
items.excerpt: It would be one thing if the arguments for expanding fossil fuels were geostrategic or economic. The public could weigh the projects and forecasts against protection of lives, species and livelihoods. Instead, the political pronouncements have been corrosive.

items.title: BC student fought her school board for composting and recycling
items.excerpt: In Grade 10, Melody Silva began pressing her Saltspring Island, BC, school to provide plastic recycling and composting. To her frustration and despite a strong economic argument and widespread student and community support, the school board remains mostly intransigent.

items.title: Fast-tracked pipeline adds pressure for Vancouver port expansion
items.excerpt: Government and independent sources alike conclude that Southern Resident killer whales are in no position to tolerate further loss of habitat or hunting grounds. A few changes in the omnibus Bill C-39 could undermine the last protections holding the project back.

items.title: Super El Niño to cause 451,000 heat deaths
items.excerpt: Climate scientists are calling the hotter temperatures resulting from El Niño a “postcard from the future.”

items.title: After arson attack, Liberal MP warns violent rhetoric puts all MPs at risk
items.excerpt: In August, a man was filmed setting vehicles on fire outside Liberal MP Salma Zahid's home in the Toronto suburb of Scarborough. She says people need to "lower the temperature" of their political rhetoric.

items.title: Another oilsands boom? Smith, Carney say this time Canada will be ready
items.excerpt: The last boom from the mid-2000s to mid-2010s came with the side-effects of cost inflation, labour scarcity and housing shortages. The prime minister and Alberta's premier say that if oilsands companies start building again — as they hope — it will be different this time around.
